ai.title: CLI distinguishes refund and closed hour errors from session takeovers
ai.summary: The Freebuff CLI now parses the server message attached to a session superseded error to determine if the session was refunded, closed at the end of the hour, or taken over by another instance. For refunded starts and closed hours, the session is ended locally and the user is shown the server message, with a hint to retry or switch models appended to refund errors. Takeover errors retain the previous behavior of marking the session as superseded. This prevents the CLI from incorrectly prompting a restart when the user simply needs to retry the request on a different model.
ai.evidence: In `cli/src/utils/error-handling.ts`, the new `getFreebuffSupersededReason` function classifies server messages for session superseded errors into 'refunded_start', 'session_closed', or 'taken_over'. In `cli/src/hooks/helpers/send-message.ts`, the `handleFreebuffGateError` function now uses this classification to end the session for refunds or closed hours, appending `FREEBUFF_REFUNDED_START_HINT` to the error message.

eli5.text: The Freebuff command-line assistant now correctly identifies when a request fails because the free model was refunded or the hour already ended, instead of mistakenly assuming another device stole your session. This helps users who code with the free assistant at no charge. If this happens to you, you will now see a helpful message telling you to retry your request or pick a different model, rather than being told to restart the entire app.

ai.summary: Freebuff CLI version 0.2.20 publishes updates including refined session error messaging and a new deterministic compaction mode. The CLI now parses the server message for session_superseded errors to distinguish between refunded model starts, closed hours, and concurrent instance takeovers, showing specific recovery hints for the first two cases. The release cleans up the agent definitions by removing the "fast" mode and related validation options from the base orchestrator, simplifying how tasks are planned and executed. ai.title: SDK treats 503 model capacity refusals as final
ai.summary: The SDK model provider now classifies HTTP 503 responses carrying the `model_at_capacity` error code as final, non-retryable refusals. Previously, the AI SDK's retry loop treated all 503 responses as transient, causing it to re-queue the step and retry up to four times with backoff before failing. This change stops the retry loop on the first refusal, immediately surfacing the server's capacity message or the SDK's fallback copy to the client.
ai.evidence: In `sdk/src/impl/model-provider.ts`, a new entry with `status: 503` and `error: 'model_at_capacity'` is added to the `FINAL_REFUSALS` array, with a corresponding fallback message. The `throwIfFinalRefusal` function now evaluates this status and error code to throw a non-retryable `APICallError`.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not indicate whether the CLI has been updated to specifically parse and display the `model_at_capacity` error code in its UI, though it will now receive the error immediately rather than after a failed retry sequence.

eli5.text: When a free AI model is too busy to start a task, the assistant now tells you immediately instead of waiting in line four times. This affects people using free AI models who hit a busy moment. You will see a message telling you the model is full and to try later or pick a different one, which saves you from an unnecessary wait.
